title: MSPipe: Efficient Temporal GNN Training via Staleness-Aware Pipeline

problem.claim: Memory-based temporal GNNs must iteratively read and update node memory according to temporal dependencies, creating substantial overhead and limiting training throughput.

gap.claim: Optimizations for static GNNs do not directly address the training paradigm, architecture, memory module, and temporal-dependency challenges of memory-based temporal GNNs.

contributions.claim: MSPipe is a general framework for efficient memory-based temporal GNN training that targets higher throughput while maintaining model accuracy.
MSPipe integrates staleness into the memory module and uses online pipeline scheduling to break temporal dependencies with minimal staleness while delaying memory fetching for fresher states.
MSPipe includes a staleness mitigation mechanism and provides convergence analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the scheduling approach avoids stalling the MTGNN training stage and resource contention.
The authors report that MSPipe maintains the same convergence rate as vanilla sampling-based GNN training.
Experiments report up to 2.45× speed-up without sacrificing accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Memory-based temporal GNNs use node memory to retain long-term temporal dependencies and can outperform memory-less counterparts.
Temporal memory reading and updating introduces overhead and limits training throughput.
Static-GNN optimizations are not effective for the distinct architecture and temporal dependencies of memory-based temporal GNNs.
MSPipe combines staleness-aware memory handling, online pipeline scheduling, delayed fetching, and staleness mitigation.
The authors report convergence-rate preservation and up to 2.45× speed-up without sacrificing accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Introducing a fixed staleness bound may cause suboptimal performance and poor generalizability across models and datasets.

interpretation.claim: Staleness controls should adapt to runtime or workload conditions rather than rely solely on a universal predefined bound.

application.claim: For systems with dependency-constrained state updates, use online scheduling to trade limited staleness for throughput while seeking fresher state when possible.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when online scheduling is preferable across specific models, datasets, hardware, or workloads.

unknowns: Specific datasets, models, hardware, baselines, and experimental settings are not provided.
The convergence-analysis assumptions and proof details are not provided.
The scheduling algorithm and staleness-mitigation mechanism are not described in implementation detail.
The distribution of speed-ups and accuracy measurements beyond the reported maximum are not provided.
